$comment: Every native library that ships inside TrestleBoard and did not come from Microsoft, on the
assets-src/fonts/fonts.json precedent (PLAN.md §11 M14) and the assets-src/dictionaries one
after it. PLAN.md §12 gate 22 names 'the PDFium native library' by name, and until M74 (f) it
was the one asset in the app with no entry anywhere: no provenance, no hash, no licence a user
What is checked, and where: PdfiumLicenceTests (tests/PdfPages.Tests) recomputes the SHA-256 of
the licence file out of this manifest, asserts the same text is embedded in the assembly, and
asserts that every native binary this manifest names is one Docnet.Core actually ships. The
binaries themselves are NOT in this repository — they arrive from the NuGet package named
below, which is why their hashes are recorded here rather than recomputed from the tree.

note: The managed wrapper is MIT. The native library inside it is PDFium, which is not — that is
what this manifest is for. Version 2.6.0 is pinned in Directory.Packages.props.

natives.name: PDFium
usedFor: Turning one page of somebody else's PDF into a picture, at import time only
the import ever sees a PDF, so PDFium is never on the path that draws a page or writes one.
natives.licence: BSD-3-Clause (PDFium itself) plus the terms of its bundled third-party code
licenceNote: Not a single named licence, for the same reason the spelling dictionary is not: PDFium
statically links libpng, LibTIFF, agg23, FreeType, lcms, OpenJPEG, zlib, libjpeg-turbo, the
IJG notices and ICU, and each of those carries its own notice. Eleven notices in one file,
which is why the whole file ships rather than an SPDX id. BSD-3-Clause and Apache-2.0 both
require the notice to accompany a binary distribution, so this is a condition of shipping,
Why it is vendored rather than taken from the package at build time. Docnet.Core does put
a file called LICENSE in runtimes/<rid>/native/, and NuGet does copy it: a
`dotnet publish -r win-x64 --self-contained` lands it in the publish root as a bare file
named `LICENSE`, beside TrestleBoard.App.exe, with nothing on it or near it saying which of
the twenty-odd packages it belongs to — and any other package shipping a native `LICENSE`
would overwrite it, last one wins. A notice nobody can attribute and nobody is shown does
not discharge an attribution clause. Embedded in the assembly and surfaced under

changesMade: One byte. The upstream file is otherwise UTF-8 but carries a single Latin-1 0xA9 (a
copyright sign) at offset 18556, which makes the whole file invalid UTF-8 and turns that
one character into a replacement glyph on screen. It is written as U+00A9 in UTF-8 here.
Nothing else differs — no reflowing, no reordering, no omissions.
The osx-x64 and osx-arm64 copies carry the same eleven notices with every line prefixed
'// '. Same terms, same text; the un-prefixed copy is the one a person can read.
